section: Ambedkar's social thought - annihilation of caste, state socialism, conversion to Buddhism
subsections: Thoughts on Linguistic States - views on reorganisation

accepted.s: In which year was Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's work titled “Thoughts on Linguistic States” published?
accepted.x: “Thoughts on Linguistic States” was published in 1955.
accepted.tq: Use the direct year-recall approach for a dated work.
accepted.sec: Thoughts on Linguistic States - views on reorganisation

accepted.s: Which one of the following best represents Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's position on the relationship between language and states?
o: He accepted “one state, one language” but not “one language, one state”.
He supported “one language, one state” but rejected “one state, one language”.
He supported both “one state, one language” and “one language, one state”.
He rejected both linguistic principles in favour of administrative states.
accepted.x: Ambedkar accepted the principle of one state, one language, but did not accept the principle of one language, one state.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two similar-sounding linguistic principles instead of reversing their order.
accepted.sec: Thoughts on Linguistic States - views on reorganisation

accepted.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar warned against the creation of huge states and proposed the division of which of the following states?
o: Maharashtra, Gujarat and Rajasthan
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh
Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
Punjab, Haryana and West Bengal
accepted.x: Ambedkar warned against huge states and proposed splitting Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Test the exact membership of a named list.
accepted.sec: Thoughts on Linguistic States - views on reorganisation

accepted.s:
With reference to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's views on the reorganisation of states, consider the following statements:
1. He proposed dividing Maharashtra into smaller units.
2. He supported the creation of huge states for administrative convenience.
3. He suggested Hyderabad as a second capital of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because Ambedkar warned against huge states rather than supporting them.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses Ambedkar's warning against huge states.
accepted.sec: Thoughts on Linguistic States - views on reorganisation

accepted.s: Which city did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar suggest as a second capital of India?
o: Hyderabad
Mumbai
Nagpur
New Delhi
accepted.x: Ambedkar suggested Hyderabad as a second capital of India.
accepted.tq: Test a specific place associated with a constitutional and administrative proposal.
accepted.sec: Thoughts on Linguistic States - views on reorganisation

accepted.s: On 24 March 2026, the Supreme Court ruling concerning the loss of Scheduled Caste status after religious conversion was delivered by which of the following combination of judges?
o: Justice Manmohan and Justice P.K. Mishra
Justice P.K. Mishra and Justice Manmohan in a case unrelated to Scheduled Caste status
Justice P.K. Mishra and Justice Manmohan, sitting with a different constitutional bench
Justice P.K. Mishra and Justice Manmohan
accepted.x: The ruling on 24 March 2026 was delivered by Justices P.K. Mishra and Manmohan. The case concerned the effect of religious conversion on Scheduled Caste status.
accepted.tq: Match the precise date with the named judicial authorities.

accepted.s: According to the Supreme Court ruling of 24 March 2026, conversion out of which of the following religions results in the immediate loss of Scheduled Caste status under Clause 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950?
o: Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism
Hinduism, Jainism or Buddhism
Sikhism, Buddhism or Christianity
Hinduism, Islam or Christianity
accepted.x: The ruling held that conversion out of Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism leads to immediate loss of Scheduled Caste status under Clause 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact religious categories and the constitutional provision involved.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs correctly indicates the years in which Sikhs and Buddhists, respectively, were included for the purposes of Scheduled Caste status under the relevant constitutional order?
o: Sikhs—1956; Buddhists—1990
Sikhs—1950; Buddhists—1956
Sikhs—1956; Buddhists—1956
Sikhs—1990; Buddhists—1956
accepted.x: Sikhs were included in 1956, while Buddhists were added in 1990.
accepted.tq: Separate two close constitutional dates by testing their correct sequence.

accepted.s: The Supreme Court case concerning the effect of religious conversion on Scheduled Caste status, which originated in Andhra Pradesh, is known as:
o: Maneka Gandhi case
Kesavananda Bharati case
Indra Sawhney case
Chinthada Anand case
accepted.x: The case that came from Andhra Pradesh was the Chinthada Anand case.
accepted.tq: Use the case-name clue to identify the specific legal matter.

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the wider significance attributed to Ambedkar's approach to caste and religious conversion?
o: It shifted the anti-caste struggle from reform within Hinduism towards rights, law and religious exit.
It confined the anti-caste struggle to reform within Hinduism בלבד.
It treated religious conversion as unrelated to social equality.
It replaced legal rights with a purely cultural campaign against caste.
accepted.x: The significance lay in moving the anti-caste struggle from reform within Hinduism to rights, law and the possibility of religious exit.
accepted.tq: Apply the stated significance to distinguish a broad social-legal interpretation from narrow alternatives.

accepted.s: The Hindu described Ambedkar's 1956 conversion as which of the following?
o: The most symbolically powerful conversion in modern India
The final constitutional settlement of the caste question
The first legally recognised mass conversion in modern India
The beginning of linguistic reorganisation in modern India
accepted.x: The Hindu described Ambedkar's 1956 conversion as the most symbolically powerful in modern India.
accepted.tq: Test the precise description attached to a historically significant event.

accepted.s: The Scheduled Caste status ruling discussed in relation to Andhra Pradesh arose from the case of:
o: An Andhra Pradesh pastor under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
An Andhra Pradesh judge under the Representation of the People Act
An Andhra Pradesh legislator under the Citizenship Act
An Andhra Pradesh pastor under the Protection of Civil Rights Act בלבד
accepted.x: The ruling arose from an Andhra Pradesh pastor's case under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
accepted.tq: Identify both the litigant's description and the statute involved.
